descriptionChirho: A chiliarchos is a Roman military officer commanding approximately one thousand soldiers, equivalent to a tribunus militum (military tribune). In the NT, this term appears primarily in Acts 21-23 referring to Claudius Lysias, the tribune of the Jerusalem garrison who arrested Paul, and also in John 18:12 (the commander who arrested Jesus), Mark 6:21 (Herod's banquet guests), Acts 25:23 (at Agrippa's audience), and Revelation 6:15 and 19:18 (in apocalyptic contexts listing social ranks). All occurrences across languages converge on the same referent: Arabic 'al-amir,' Hebrew 'sar ha-elef / sar ha-meah,' Korean 'cheonbujang,' Hindi 'sahasrapati,' German 'Tribun,' Spanish 'tribuno/comandante.' The singular/plural and case variations (nominative, genitive, dative, accusative) are purely grammatical and do not indicate distinct senses.
